title: Blackened Salmon Sweet Potato Bowls
seoTitle: Blackened Salmon Sweet Potato Bowls | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Cajun-blackened salmon over roasted sweet potato and greens with a cooling yogurt drizzle
subtitle: Cajun-blackened salmon over roasted sweet potato and greens with a cooling yogurt drizzle
description: Salmon fillets get a bold blackening seasoning and a hard sear, then sit over roasted sweet potato and sautéed greens with a cool lemon-yogurt drizzle to balance the heat.

steps.title: Roast the sweet potato
steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss sweet potato cubes with 2 tablespoons oil, salt, and pepper on a sheet pan and roast 22–25 minutes, turning once, until tender and browned at the edges. Target oven/smoker temperature: 425°F.

steps.title: Mix the blackening seasoning
steps.instruction: Combine smoked paprika, garlic powder, cayenne, thyme, salt, and pepper in a small bowl. Pat salmon portions dry, then coat evenly on both sides — dry fish takes seasoning and sears better than wet fish.

steps.title: Sear the salmon
steps.instruction: Heat remaining oil in a large skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Sear salmon skin-side up first 3–4 minutes until a dark crust forms, flip, and cook 3 more minutes to 130–135°F for medium.

steps.title: Wilt the greens
steps.instruction: In the same skillet, add garlic and spinach in batches, tossing 2–3 minutes just until wilted. Season lightly with salt — the salmon and sauce both carry plenty of flavor already.

steps.title: Mix the lemon-yogurt sauce
steps.instruction: Stir Greek yogurt with lemon juice, dill, and a pinch of salt until smooth. Keep it cold in a squeeze bottle so it stays thick and cooling against the spiced fish.

steps.title: Hold and build the bowls
steps.instruction: Keep salmon loosely covered and sweet potato warm in a 200°F oven. Layer sweet potato and spinach in each bowl, top with a portion of salmon, and finish with a drizzle of yogurt sauce. Target oven/smoker temperature: 200°F.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover blackened salmon — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool blackened salmon and hot components in a shallow baking dish within two hours — food left out too long isn't safe to eat. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Prep tip: Pat salmon completely dry before seasoning — moisture is the enemy of a real blackened crust.
Rookie tip: Pull salmon a shade under your target temperature; it keeps cooking a bit while it rests.
Use cod or tilapia if the hall doesn't have salmon on hand — the seasoning still works well.
Keep cayenne on the lower end if the crew doesn't run hot on spice; the smoked paprika still carries flavor.
tonightSpread: Main: Blackened salmon sweet potato bowls
Sides: Simple cucumber salad, lemon wedges
Condiments: Extra yogurt sauce, hot sauce
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool salmon and sweet potato in shallow pans within two hours; reheat salmon gently, not on high heat.
Store the yogurt sauce separately — it keeps well cold for up to 3 days.
Flake leftover salmon over greens for a fast next-day lunch instead of reheating it whole.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It gives crews who are tired of chicken and beef a genuinely satisfying fish option with real crust and spice, and the sweet potato base makes it filling instead of light and forgettable.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: roast sweet potato up to two days ahead; the yogurt sauce holds 3 days. Storage: keep salmon, sweet potato, and greens separate. Reheating: gently reheat salmon covered at 275°F just until warm — high heat dries it out fast.
substitutions: Use cod, tilapia, or trout in place of salmon.
Use sour cream thinned with a little water if Greek yogurt isn't on hand.
Swap spinach for kale or broccolini.
